greek: Ἀπάρας δὲ Ισραηλ, αὐτὸς καὶ πάντα τὰ αὐτοῦ, ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ ὅρκου καὶ ἔθυσεν θυσίαν τῷ θεῷ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Ισαακ.
hint: Israel sets out with all he has, comes to the Well of the Oath, and sacrifices to the God of Isaac.

notes.text: The well of the oath: the Greek renders the name, as at 21:32, 26:23 and 28:10. The Hebrew has bĕʾērâ šābaʿ, Beersheba.
The article over a genitive pronoun: the things of him, all he had.

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")
(Ισαακ, from Hebrew Yiṣḥāq, "he laughs")

greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς Ισραηλ ἐν ὁράματι τῆς νυκτὸς εἴπας Ιακωβ, Ιακωβ. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Τί ἐστιν;
hint: God speaks to Israel in a night vision, calling him Jacob twice; Jacob answers.

notes.text: The aorist participle of λέγω, with the first-aorist ending: saying.
What is it? The Hebrew has hinnēnî, here I am.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] to [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[in that which is seen|within, inside of, and by means of that which is seen and a sight and spectacle|ἐν; ὅραμα]] [[of the night-season|of the night-season, of the night, of the watches of the night, of the dark of night, of the night of death|νύξ]] [[having said|having said, having spoken, having declared, having called by name, having told|λέγω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]]. the one [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] what is?

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: λέγων Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου· μὴ φοβοῦ καταβῆναι εἰς Αἴγυπτον· εἰς γὰρ ἔθνος μέγα ποιήσω σε ἐκεῖ,
hint: God tells him not to fear going down to Egypt, where he will make him a great nation.

notes.text: The God of your fathers, plural. The Hebrew has hāʾēl ʾĕlōhê ʾābîkā, God, the God of your father.
φοβέομαι with an infinitive: do not fear to go down.

greek: καὶ ἐγὼ καταβήσομαι μετὰ σοῦ εἰς Αἴγυπτον, καὶ ἐγὼ ἀναβιβάσω σε εἰς τέλος, καὶ Ιωσηφ ἐπιβαλεῖ τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου.
hint: God will go down with him and bring him up again, and Joseph will close his eyes.

notes.text: εἰς with τέλος, which Middle Liddell gives adverbially as at last. The Hebrew has gam-ʿālōh, surely bringing up.
Middle Liddell's τέλος runs from fulfilment and end to office, taxes and rites; its examples' pieces are in NOT_SENSES.

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: ἀνέστη δὲ Ιακωβ ἀπὸ τοῦ φρέατος τοῦ ὅρκου, καὶ ἀνέλαβον οἱ υἱοὶ Ισραηλ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν καὶ τὴν ἀποσκευὴν καὶ τὰς γυναῖκας αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τὰς ἁμάξας, ἃς ἀπέστειλεν Ιωσηφ ἆραι αὐτόν,

notes.text: ἀποσκευή, the removal, the baggage, as at 43:8. The Hebrew has ṭappām, their little ones.

reading: [[stood up|stood up, rose, rose to fight against, rose to go and set out|ἀνίστημι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the well|of the well, of the tank and cistern and reservoir, of the oil jar|φρέαρ]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears and witness of an oath, of the oath|ὅρκος]], and [[took up|took up, took into one's hands, took on board ship, took with one, took upon themselves and assumed, learned by rote, got back and regained and recovered, retrieved and made good, restored and repaired and regained strength and revived, took up again and resumed and recollected, pulled short up and checked and called back, gained quite over and won over|ἀναλαμβάνω]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of them and [[the removal|the removal and riddance, the baggage, the household stuff, the ordure and filth|ἀποσκευή]] and [[the women|the women, the mistresses and ladies, the wives and spouses, the mortal women|γυνή]] of them [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[the wagons|the wagons and wains, the wagon-loads of, the carriages of the plough, the Charles' wains, the Great Bears|ἅμαξα]], which [[sent off|sent off, sent away and banished, despatched, went away and departed|ἀποστέλλω]] [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[to take up|to take up and raise and lift up, to bear and sustain, to raise up and exalt, to excite, to extol and exaggerate, to lift and take away and remove, to take off and kill|αἴρω]] him,

greek: καὶ ἀναλαβόντες τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτῶν καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν κτῆσιν, ἣν ἐκτήσαντο ἐν γῇ Χανααν, εἰσῆλθον εἰς Αἴγυπτον, Ιακωβ καὶ πᾶν τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτοῦ,
hint: They take their goods and everything they acquired in Canaan, and Jacob comes into Egypt with all his offspring.

notes.text: The verb is plural, and Jacob with all his offspring stands after it as its subject.

greek: υἱοὶ καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτοῦ, θυγατέρες καὶ θυγατέρες τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ· καὶ πᾶν τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἤγαγεν εἰς Αἴγυπτον.
hint: Sons and grandsons, daughters and granddaughters: he brings all his offspring to Egypt.

notes.text: θυγάτηρ, a daughter, one translation: plain text, as υἱός is.

greek: Ταῦτα δὲ τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ τῶν εἰσελθόντων εἰς Αἴγυπτον. Ιακωβ καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ· πρωτότοκος Ιακωβ Ρουβην.
hint: The list of Israel's sons who entered Egypt begins with Reuben, Jacob's firstborn.

notes.text: The article with the aorist participle, agreeing with τῶν υἱῶν: of the ones who went in.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the names|the names, the fames, the mere names, the phrases and expressions|ὄνομα]] of the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[of the ones having gone in|of the ones having gone in, of the ones having gone into and entered, of the ones having come into, of the ones having come in, of the ones having come upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Αἴγυπτον]]. [[name:Ιακωβ]] and the sons of him; first-born of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[name:Ρουβην]].

names.gloss: (Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Ρουβην· Ενωχ καὶ Φαλλους, Ασρων καὶ Χαρμι.

notes.text: The Hebrew has Ḥănôk, Pallûʾ, Ḥeṣrôn and Karmî.

(Φαλλους, from Hebrew Pallûʾ, of uncertain meaning)

(Χαρμι, from Hebrew Karmî, usually connected with kerem, "vineyard")

The Hebrew has Ṣōḥar.
Χανανῖτις, the woman of Canaan, with the article: the Canaanite woman.

notes.text: The Hebrew has Gēršôn, Qĕhāt and Mĕrārî.

reading: sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Λευι]]; [[name:Γηρσων]], [[name:Κααθ]] and [[name:Μεραρι]].

hint: These are Leah's descendants born to Jacob in Mesopotamia, with Dinah: thirty-three in all.

notes.text: In Mesopotamia of Syria, as at 33:18. The Hebrew has bĕpaddan ʾărām.
ψυχή, whose first sense is breath, counts persons here, as the Hebrew nepeš does.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] sons of [[name:Λειας]], which [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, begot, produced and yielded|τίκτω]] to the [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Μεσοποταμίᾳ]] of the [[name:Συρίας]], and [[name:Διναν]] the daughter of him; [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the breaths|the breaths, the lives, the spirits, life and death, the ghosts, the departed souls|ψυχή]], sons and daughters, thirty three. —

notes.text: What is your work? The Hebrew has mah-maʿăśêkem, what are your deeds.

reading: [[if haply|if haply, if|ἐάν]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] [[may call|may call, may summon, may call to himself, may invite|καλέω]] you [[name:Φαραω]] and [[may say|may say, may speak, may declare, may call by name, may tell|λέγω]] to you what [[the work|the work, the business, the deeds, the action, the works of industry and tilled lands|ἔργον]] of you is?

greek: ἐρεῖτε Ἄνδρες κτηνοτρόφοι ἐσμὲν οἱ παῖδές σου ἐκ παιδὸς ἕως τοῦ νῦν, καὶ ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, ἵνα κατοικήσητε ἐν γῇ Γεσεμ Ἀραβίᾳ· βδέλυγμα γάρ ἐστιν Αἰγυπτίοις πᾶς ποιμὴν προβάτων.
hint: They are to say they have kept livestock since youth, to settle in Goshen, for shepherds are abhorrent to Egyptians.

notes.text: In the land of Gesem, in Arabia, with Ἀραβίᾳ in the dative beside γῇ. The Hebrew has bĕʾereṣ gōšen.
παῖς without the article, from a child: from childhood.
ἕως with the article and νῦν: until now.

reading: [[you will say|you will say, you will speak, you will declare, you will call by name, you will tell|λέγω]] [[men|men, men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] [[keeping cattle|keeping cattle and pastoral|κτηνοτρόφος]] we are [[the children|the children, the sons, the daughters, the grandchildren, the boys and youths and lads, the girls and maidens, the slaves and servants and men and maids|παῖς]] of you [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of child|of child, of son, of daughter, of grandchild, of boy and youth and lad, of girl and maiden, of slave and servant and man and maid|παῖς]] [[until|until, till, while and so long as|ἕως]] of the thing [[now at this very time|now at this very time, now, of the present, the present time, just now and but now, as it is and as the case now stands, in this case|νῦν]], and we and [[the fathers|the fathers, the grandfathers|πατήρ]] of us, [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[you may dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|you may dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), you may settle in and colonise, you may inhabit, you may settle and dwell, you may lie and be situate|κατοικέω]] [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, ground|ἐν; γῆ]] of [[name:Γεσεμ]] to [[name:Ἀραβίᾳ]]; [[an abomination|an abomination, an idol|βδέλυγμα]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] is to [[name:Αἰγυπτίοις]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[herdsman|herdsman, shepherd, captain and chief|ποιμήν]] [[of things that walk forward|of things that walk forward, of cattle, of flocks and herds, of horses, of small cattle, of sheep|πρόβατον]].

names.gloss: (Γεσεμ, from Hebrew Gōšen, of uncertain meaning)
(Ἀραβία, the Greek name of the land of the Ἄραβες, the Arabs)
(Αἰγύπτιος, the man of Αἴγυπτος, Egypt)
